Q1.student_answer: In Object Oriented Programming (OOP) inheritance is a concept that allows a class to acquire properties and behaviours from another class. We can create a new class from an existing class. It promotes code reusability and better organization. The types of inheritance are: Single inheritance - Here, a subclass is derived from only one super class. It inherits the properties and behaviour of a single-parent class. It is also known as simple inheritance. Multilevel inheritance - Here, a derived class will be inheriting a base class and the derived class also acts as the base class for other classes. Hierarchical Inheritance - Here, more than one subclass is inherited from a single base class, that is, more than one derived class is created from a single base class. Multiple inheritance - Here, one class can have more than one super class and inherit features from all parent classes. Hybrid inheritance - In Java, we can achieve hybrid inheritance only through interfaces if we want to involve multiple inheritance to implement hybrid inheritance.

criteria_breakdown.description: Inheritance is the OOP mechanism by which a derived class acquires properties and behaviours from a base class.
Correctly name and briefly explain any three types of inheritance.
criteria_breakdown.diagnostics: Matched 5/3 options: ['single inheritance', 'multiple inheritance', 'multilevel inheritance', 'hierarchical inheritance', 'hybrid inheritance']

Q2.question_text: Explain Object Oriented Programming and its characteristics.
Q2.student_answer: Object Oriented Programming (OOP) is a programming paradigm based on the concepts of objects that contain data (fields) and behaviour (methods). It is used to improve code reusability, enhance maintainability and scalability, make programs easier to manage and understand, and closely model real-world entities. Characteristics of OOP include Class, which is the blueprint or template used to create objects and defines properties and behaviours; Object, which is an instance of a class representing a real-world entity. The four pillars of OOP are Inheritance, Polymorphism, Encapsulation and Abstraction. Inheritance allows a class to inherit properties and behaviours from another class. Polymorphism allows objects of different classes to be treated as objects of a common base class. Encapsulation bundles data and methods into a single unit known as a class and access modifiers control access. Abstraction hides complex code while exposing essential parts.

criteria_breakdown.description: Object-oriented programming is a programming paradigm based on objects that bundle data and behaviour.
Encapsulation binds data and methods into a single unit and restricts direct access to some components.
Abstraction hides implementation details and complexity while exposing only essential features.
Inheritance allows a class to acquire properties and behaviours from another class and enables reuse.
Polymorphism allows a function, method, or operator to behave differently depending on the object or context.

Q3.student_answer: Polymorphism is one of the fundamental concepts of OOP that allows a single entity to take multiple forms. It enables the same method or interface to behave differently depending on the object involved. Types of polymorphism include compile-time polymorphism, also known as static polymorphism, where the method to be executed is determined during compilation. Method overloading allows multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists. Runtime polymorphism occurs when a method is resolved during program execution. Method overriding occurs when a subclass provides its own implementation of a method already defined in its superclass.

criteria_breakdown.description: Polymorphism means many forms and allows a function, method, or operator to behave differently depending on the object or arguments.
Compile-time or static polymorphism is achieved through function or operator overloading and is resolved at compile time.
Run-time or dynamic polymorphism is achieved through method overriding and is resolved at run time.

Q4.student_answer: A class is a blueprint that defines data and behaviour for objects. It groups related fields and methods in a single unit. Memory for instance members is allocated when an object is created, while static members are allocated when the class is loaded in memory. An object is an instance of a class created to access its data and operations. Each object holds its state.

criteria_breakdown.description: A class is a user-defined blueprint or template defining properties and behaviours common to its objects.
An object is a real-world instance of a class with its own actual property values.
